memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son. But God said to him, "Do not be so distressed about the boy and your slave woman. Listen to whatever Sarah tells you, because it is through Isaac that your offspring will be reckoned." - Gen 21:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham is torn. Sarah wants Hagar and Ishmael sent away, and "the matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son." He loved Ishmael. This was no easy decision; it cut at his heart. And into his distress, God speaks - not with harshness, but with reassurance and direction.

Notice first that God acknowledges Abraham's pain. "Do not be so distressed." God doesn't dismiss the anguish of a father's heart; He meets it with tenderness. When we bring our distress to God, we find not a cold command but a caring word. He understands the things that grieve us.

Then God gives direction, clarifying His purpose: "it is through Isaac that your offspring will be reckoned." God had a plan, and He was steering the family toward it. What felt to Abraham like an impossible, heartbreaking choice was, in God's hands, part of His larger redemptive purpose - the line of promise that would lead, in time, to Christ.

Sometimes God asks us to release something or someone precious, and it distresses us greatly. In those moments, we can trust that God both feels our pain and holds a purpose we cannot yet see. His guidance may lead us through heartache, but never without His care and never apart from His good plan. "Trust in the Lord with all your heart... and he will make your paths straight" (Prov 3:5-6). Bring your distress to the God who directs with love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is God asking you to release something precious that distresses you?
- Can you trust that God both feels your pain and holds a good purpose?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, when hard decisions distress my heart, thank You that You meet me with tenderness, not coldness. Help me trust that You feel my pain and hold a purpose I cannot yet see. Guide me with Your love.
Amen.
